---
title: Change or delete a type
description: Check a change to a registered type, replace its definition, and delete a type nothing uses.
---

The examples change the receipt type from [Define a type](/build/define-a-type), with the key that guide made. Each call sends `receipt.json` as that guide left it, and `definition` is that file read in, as [Register the type](/build/define-a-type#register-the-type) shows. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows. In the Swift examples, `api` is a `Client` made as [the Swift SDK](/swift-sdk/server-calls#the-api-client) shows, and `receiptURL` is the file's location. [What your key needs](/build/define-a-type#what-your-key-needs) lists the permissions each call takes.

## Check the change

A replacement **sends the whole definition**, so change the file and send all of it. To add an optional category, add `"version": 1` and this field to `receipt.json`:

```json
"category": { "type": "enum", "enum_values": ["travel", "meals", "supplies"] }
```

To see what would change first, normalize the file. Normalizing changes nothing, and any key can do it, so a connector uses it to decide whether its type needs registering or replacing:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types normalize --file receipt.json
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /types/normalize
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

<the contents of receipt.json>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/types/normalize", { body: definition });
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let normalized = try await api.check(itemType: definition)
```

The answer's `type` is your definition with its defaults written out, such as `required: false` and `searchable: true`, and `registered_type` is the registered one in the same form. Compare those two, not `resolved_type`, which adds every field the registered type inherits. Both registered forms are `null` when the identifier isn't registered. A key Marfa doesn't read, anywhere in a definition, is refused `400 invalid_schema`, naming it.

## Replace the type

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types replace app.example.receipt --file receipt.json
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PUT /types/app.example.receipt
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

<the contents of receipt.json>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PUT("/types/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id: "app.example.receipt" } },
  body: definition,
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let update = try JSONDecoder().decode(
    Components.Schemas.TypeDefinitionUpdate.self, from: Data(contentsOf: receiptURL))
_ = try await api.replace(itemType: "app.example.receipt", with: update)
```

Marfa answers `200` with the type as it stored it. **Send the `version` every time:** a replacement without one sets it back to 0. You can't replace or delete a type Marfa ships: that's refused `403 core_type_immutable`.

A replacement **changes no item you already hold**:

- **A property you made required** is checked the next time the item's properties are written.
- **A property you removed** is gone from the type, but items keep their values for it, and a later write isn't refused for them.
- **A rule you tightened,** such as a lower `maximum`, leaves the values items hold. A write is refused only when it changes that property.

**A replacement keeps the icon the owner chose** for the type ([the owner's icon](/catalog/display-hints#the-owners-icon)). Sending back what [Get a type](/api-reference/types/getType) answered changes only what you changed: a display hint you send with the value the type inherits isn't stored, so the type keeps following its parent.

A change to `title_field` or `body_field` changes how the server and every device [name and preview](/catalog/display-hints#names-and-previews) the type's items. The body field holds up to 1,000,000 characters by default ([Field kinds](/catalog/field-kinds#kinds)), so moving the hint to another field gives that field the limit. A longer value the old body field holds stays readable, but the item's next write of it is refused `400 invalid_properties` until it's shortened.

**A type's identifier never changes.** To rename a type, register the new one, [move the items](/build/move-items-to-another-type) to it, then delete the old one. A move also changes the folders, views and webhooks that name the old type.

## Delete the type

Marfa deletes a type that **no item holds**, in any state, the bin included; that no folder, view, webhook or [table](/build/tables) column names; and that no other type names as its parent or in `compatible_with`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types delete app.example.receipt
```

```http tab="HTTP"
DELETE /types/app.example.receipt
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.DELETE("/types/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id: "app.example.receipt" } },
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
try await api.delete(itemType: "app.example.receipt")
```

Otherwise Marfa refuses it:

| Refusal | When | What's in `details` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `409 type_has_subtypes` | Another type names it as its parent. | `subtype_ids` |
| `422 compatible_with_violation` | Another type names it in `compatible_with`. | `dependent_type_ids` |
| `409 type_in_use` | Items hold it, or a folder, view, webhook or table column names it. | `item_count`, `settings` and `columns` |

For `type_in_use`, **[move the items to another type](/build/move-items-to-another-type) first:** the move changes the folders, views and webhooks too. A setting your key can't read is named by its `kind` and `field` alone, without its `id`. A key or app whose type map names the type doesn't stop a delete.

<Callout type="warn" title="A forced delete blocks writes to the items">
`force=true` (the CLI's `--force`) deletes a type that items still hold or a setting names. A subtype or a `compatible_with` claim still blocks it. The items and settings stay, and the items are still read, listed and found. But a write of an item's properties, tier or time is refused `400 unknown_type` until the type is registered again. You can still tag the items, archive them or move them to the bin.
</Callout>

The rules behind this guide are in the [types](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/types.md) chapter of the contract.
